title: UniboostMintDebtHook.scale derived from the hook's own ctor primeToken_ with no on-chain tie to the dispatcher primeToken(); decimals mismatch mis-scales all debt
description: UniboostMintDebtHook takes dispatcher_ and primeToken_ as two separate, same-typed address args and bakes scale = 10**(18 - primeToken_.decimals()) as an immutable at ctor line 89. There is no on-chain cross-validation that primeToken_ equals the dispatcher's actual _primeToken (Uniboost.sol:89). If the owner passes a primeToken_ whose decimals() differ from the dispatcher's real prime, every onDispatch accrues debt at the wrong scale. Non-obvious because the M-03/M-04 fixes would lead an owner to assume the scale is bound to the dispatcher.
impact: Two directions. UNDER-scale (hook primeToken_ has MORE decimals than the real dispatcher prime): debt under-stated => fails safe (over-backed, no loss). OVER-scale (hook primeToken_ has FEWER decimals than the real dispatcher prime): debt over-stated => a later pull() mints MORE phUSD than ratio*amount warrants => UNBACKED phUSD over-mint. The over-scale direction is the Law-1 tail that mandates KEEPING this finding even at Low. Decimal MATH itself is correct/guarded (d<=18, M-03 generalization) and is explicitly NOT re-raised.
attackPath: 1. Owner deploys UniboostMintDebtHook passing dispatcher_ and primeToken_ as two separate, same-typed address args.
2. Owner passes a primeToken_ whose decimals() differ from the dispatcher's actual _primeToken (Uniboost.sol:89) -- both args type-check, neither is on-chain cross-validated.
3. scale = 10**(18 - wrongDecimals) is baked immutable at line 89.
4. Every onDispatch accrues debt at the wrong scale; if scale is too large, pull() later mints unbacked phUSD.
recommendation: Add a constructor assertion: require(IERC20Metadata(IUniboost(dispatcher_).primeToken()).decimals() == d) (or derive d directly from the dispatcher's primeToken()), removing the dual-arg ambiguity.

classification.plausibility: n/a (owner deploy-config dependent, not an attacker scenario)
classification.likelihood: low; requires a deploy-time mismatch of two owner-supplied args in a single atomic deployment. No runtime path, no external attacker, no permissionless trigger. Mis-scale is detectable on the first dispatch (DebtAccrued amounts off by orders of magnitude).
classification.externalRequirements: None -- the only actor is the deploying owner.
classification.recoverable: Partially. scale is immutable, so an over-scaled hook must be replaced (deploy a new hook + re-wire). phUSD already over-minted via pull() during the window is the irrecoverable portion; the mis-scale is detectable before pull() if monitored.

crossRef: Open ledger L-07 (ac91a046) -- same decimal-config family on a different surface (replaceDispatcher stale price). Distinct fingerprint; do NOT merge.
borderlineNote: Deliberately-scrutinized borderline Low/Medium. Kept Low: no external requirement, no attacker, no runtime trigger; single atomic owner deploy error; detectable pre-pull. Unbacked-over-mint tail is why it is KEPT under Law-1 recall-beats-tidiness rather than dropped. Tier-3 confirmed math cannot over-mint under correct deployment, backing >=2:1.
